description:
Mountain biking is my first love — I’ve been racing mountain bikes for over 35 years, going back to the days when fully rigid was the only option. Building a Sage full suspension bike has been on my mind since the company started. It turns out a lot of customers had been asking for the same thing. The question was never whether to build it. It was what kind, and when the technology would actually let me build it the way I wanted to.

That answer arrived a few years ago, when 3D printed titanium components matured to the point where I could design what I needed instead of compromising around what was available. The result is the bike you’re looking at — a titanium full suspension XC/Downcountry mountain bike, hand-built in the USA, designed to climb fast and descend hard.

It’s been over three years of design, prototyping, and testing. We’ve finally arrived at something I’m proud to put my name on — and to give a name of its own. This is the Harbinger.

— Dave

Most full suspension titanium attempts of the past have ended up flexy, heavy, or both. We didn’t accept that as the answer.

The frame uses Grade 9 (3/2.5) US-sourced titanium tubing — the standard for high-end frame construction — blended with Grade 5 (6/4) 3D printed titanium components at every load-critical junction: upper and lower shock mounts, bottom bracket cluster, chainstay yoke, seat stay bridge, rear brake mount, and dropouts. Grade 5 is the gold standard for additive titanium manufacturing. We use an enhanced 3D printing process that yields significantly stronger components than what most other 3D-printed titanium bike parts use today.

The suspension is a single pivot flex stay design with 115mm of rear travel, paired with a 120mm fork. We deliberately chose flex stay over linkage. There are plenty of multi-link bikes in the market — building another one wasn’t going to add anything new. A single pivot flex stay in full titanium is unique. It’s simpler, it’s lighter, it’s easier to maintain, and it lets the natural ride feel of titanium come through in a way a more complex linkage system can’t.

The shock is linkage-driven to dial in the kinematics. Since the first prototype, we’ve also refined the linkage that drives the shock — cutting nearly half a pound off the rear end while keeping the same kinematic feel: firm off the top, plush in the middle, ramping up for a bottomless feel on the big hits.

Rear brake mounting has moved from IS to Post Mount, opening up compatibility across SRAM, Shimano, and TRP calipers. The rear rotor mount is now native 180mm, up from 160mm on the previous version — more braking power, and a cleaner look with no adapter needed.

Confirmed clearance for 29×2.4″ tires, front and rear.

Look closely and you’ll find the Owl embossed into the dropouts and the SAGE wordmark embossed into the chainstay yoke — small details, but ones that only make sense on a bike built this way.

The most consistent feedback we got since our time at Sea Otter — from riders and industry pros who put the bike through its paces — was that it felt laterally as stiff as the high-end carbon XC bikes they’d been on. That’s exactly what we set out to build, and it’s not something I take for granted on a first-generation titanium full suspension prototype.

The bike is aggressive XC/Downcountry. Fast uphill. Fast downhill. Fun, poppy, playful. The kind of bike that puts a smile on your face after every ride and makes you want to push a little harder the next time out.

I’m still finding the limits of this bike, and I’ve been riding it as hard as I can on technical terrain. So far it keeps coming back for more.

Harbinger is real, and it’s getting closer to production every week. Here’s where things stand and what’s still ahead.

In progress now:

Coming up:

A note on transparency: this is a prototype that is becoming a production bike. Specifications, geometry, weight, and component packages are subject to change as testing continues. We’ll update this page and notify deposit holders directly as decisions get locked in. If anything changes meaningfully between your deposit and your delivery, you’ll hear it from us first.

Harbinger will be built to order, not mass produced. There won’t be inventory sitting on a shelf, and the first batch will be shaped by who commits early.

Getting in early on a handbuilt, made-in-USA titanium full suspension bike — before the rest of the world has seen it in its final form — comes with real advantages. You get first position in the production queue. You get preferred pricing on components if you build complete. And you get a free Cerakote finish on your frame logos.

This isn’t a bike for everyone — and that’s intentional. Harbinger is a limited first production run of a handbuilt, made-in-USA, full suspension titanium mountain bike unlike anything else on the market. The customers who deposit first will be part of a small, original group of riders who define what this bike is and what it stands for.

The deposit is $1,000. It secures your place in the production queue and locks in your pre-order benefits. Pre-orders are first-come, first-served — earlier deposits get earlier delivery slots and earlier access to information. Placing a deposit is a commitment to purchasing a Sage bike: deposits are non-refundable, without exception.

Pre-order benefits include:

Frameset price: $14,000. This includes the titanium frame, rear shock, Sage titanium seatpost collar, and rear thru-axle.

Refunds and transfers. Deposits are non-refundable, without exception. Placing your deposit is a commitment to purchasing a Sage bike. If you’d like flexibility on which Sage model to build, your deposit is fully transferable to any other current Sage model — Skyline, Storm King, Optimator, or any other current model — but it does not convert back to cash.

What the deposit secures. Your $1,000 holds your place in line. It does not lock in final geometry, components, or specifications — those will be confirmed with each customer prior to your build. We’ll keep deposit holders informed of any meaningful changes as they happen. Since deposits are transferable to any Sage bike at any time, you always have the flexibility to make a different choice if Harbinger stops being the right bike for you.

When will I receive my bike?
The target remains on track for Q1 2027 for first customer deliveries, pending successful completion of testing and production validation. Earlier deposits get earlier delivery slots. We’ll communicate your estimated delivery window once the production schedule is locked in.

What sizes will be offered?
Harbinger will launch with a range of stock sizes designed to fit most riders. Sizing details will be finalized and shared with deposit holders before final production begins. Custom geometry is not offered as a standard option for this bike, but is available case-by-case for an additional charge.

What does the frameset include?
The frameset includes the titanium frame, rear shock, Sage titanium seatpost collar, and rear thru-axle.

What components will be available for complete builds?
You have real flexibility here. We’ll steer you toward premium, proven components and away from anything that will let the bike down, but the final build — drivetrain, wheels, cockpit, and finishing kit — is yours to configure. Think of it less as picking from a fixed menu and more as building the bike you actually want, with our guidance along the way.

What if specifications change between now and production?
We’ll tell you. Major changes — geometry, suspension travel, intended use — will be communicated to deposit holders directly before they go public. Because deposits are transferable to any Sage bike at any time, you always have flexibility if a change affects your decision.

Is the deposit refundable?
No. Once placed, deposits are non-refundable — no exceptions. Placing a deposit is a commitment to purchasing a Sage bike. If your plans change, your deposit is fully transferable to any other Sage model, but it does not convert back to cash.

Do I have to commit to a complete bike?
No. Pre-order customers can choose frameset only or a complete bike when their build slot comes up. Preferred component pricing applies to complete builds.

How many pre-orders are you accepting?
Harbinger is a limited first production run, as production capacity for a handbuilt, 3D-printed titanium full suspension bike is genuinely finite. We’ll communicate through our channels when the first production run is complete.

Is the $14,000 frameset price final?
Yes. Frameset pricing is confirmed at $14,000, which includes the titanium frame, rear shock, Sage titanium seatpost collar, and rear thru-axle.

Not ready to deposit but want to stay close to the project? Join the Harbinger list and you’ll be the first to know about production updates, size availability, and delivery timing.
